## Verdict

missing

## Bearer

RecordedRaceListenerService — new class, `app-phone/src/main/java/com/mgilli/hyroxtracker/sync/RecordedRaceListenerService.kt`, extending `WearableListenerService`

## Trigger

A message arriving on the Wearable Data Layer at path `/recorded-race` — nothing observes it

## Today

`:core-sync`'s `WearableRecordedRaceTransport.send` (`core-sync/src/main/kotlin/com/mgilli/core/sync/transport/WearableRecordedRaceTransport.kt`) encodes a `RecordedRacePayload` with `PayloadCodec.encode` and delivers it via `MessageChannel`/`DataLayerMessageChannel` to path `/recorded-race`. No `MessageClient.OnMessageReceivedListener` and no `WearableListenerService` is registered anywhere in `:core-sync` or `:app-phone` (grep of both finds none). `app-phone`'s manifest (`app-phone/src/main/AndroidManifest.xml`) declares no service. The message reaches the phone's Data Layer and is never read; `RaceRepository.saveRecordedRace` (`core-domain/src/main/kotlin/com/mgilli/core/domain/race/RaceRepository.kt`) is already implemented and already injectable on the phone (bound in `app-phone/src/main/java/com/mgilli/hyroxtracker/di/RepositoryModule.kt`), but nothing on the phone calls it for a race sent from the watch.

## Expected

A `WearableListenerService` in `:app-phone`, taking `RaceRepository` by Hilt injection, registers to receive messages on path `/recorded-race` and, on each one, decodes the payload's bytes and calls `RaceRepository.saveRecordedRace` with the decoded name, date, segments and completion.

This requires a second gap: `PayloadCodec` (`core-sync/src/main/kotlin/com/mgilli/core/sync/transport/PayloadCodec.kt`) is `internal` to `:core-sync` and only exposes `encode(RecordedRacePayload)` / `encode(ProfileSyncPayload)` — no `decode` function exists at all. Decoding a `RecordedRacePayload` from bytes needs a `decode` counterpart, and it needs to be reachable from `:app-phone` (not `internal`), since a platform adapter for the Data Layer belongs in `:core-sync` per the module split, while the listener itself — touching the Android `Service` lifecycle — belongs in `:app-phone`.
